## Cell Proportions- Filtering, Imputation, Plotting: N=635

This code summarizes, plots, and filters deconvoluted cell proportions for downstream analyses for sPTB (N=635) in CANDLE and PATHWAYS GAPPS.

### Upload Data and Load Packages
```{r data and packages}
#Load Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(robCompositions)

#Load Data
ciber_cells = read_csv("/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/FromBrennan/Data/CIBERSORTx_Job8_Results.csv") %>% janitor::clean_names()
load("/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/CovariateData/FilteredCovariates_CANDLEGAPPS_sPTB_122325.RData")
```

### Data Preparation
``` {r data prep}
# drop cols like correlation, rmse, and p_value, keep only the cell types 
cell_types = colnames(ciber_cells[2:28])

ciber_cells2 = ciber_cells %>% 
  dplyr::rename(pathways_id = mixture) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-p_value, -correlation, -rmse) %>%
  dplyr::filter(ciber_cells$mixture %in% CANDLE_GAPPS_sPTB_FinalCovars$pathways_id) #Reduce to only participants with full covariates

col_means <- colMeans(ciber_cells2[, 2:28], na.rm = TRUE)
col_means = as.data.frame(col_means)
col_means$cell_type <- rownames(col_means)
```

### Calculate percent cell type detected
```{r Percent Detected}
percent_detected <- sapply(cell_types, function(col_name) {
  sum(ciber_cells2[[col_name]] != 0, na.rm = TRUE) / length(ciber_cells2[[col_name]]) * 100
})

percent_detected <- data.frame(
  cell_type = cell_types,
  percent_detected = percent_detected
) %>% left_join(col_means)
percent_detected$percent_detected[is.nan(percent_detected$percent_detected)]<-0
percent_detected = percent_detected %>% arrange(percent_detected) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(mean_prop=col_means) %>% 
  mutate(mean_percent = mean_prop*100)

# Save Percent Detected
#write_csv(percent_detected, "/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/CellTypes_PercentDetected_N635_sPTB_CANDLEGAPPS_122325.csv")
```

### Collapse some cell types
We are going to try collapsing Fetal GZMK Natural Killers and Fetal GZMB Natural Killers as co-authors believe they "likely represent CD56high and CD56low/CD16high NK cell subsets based on review of gene expression and the literature". These two subsets were also very closely clustered in the UMAP from Campbell et al. 2023 paper.
```{r collapse}
ciber_cells_collapse <- ciber_cells2 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Fetal_Natural_Killer_GZMB_GZMK=fetal_gzmk_natural_killer + fetal_gzmb_natural_killer) %>%
  dplyr::select(-fetal_gzmk_natural_killer, -fetal_gzmb_natural_killer)

#Calculate percent detected after collapse
cell_type_collapse <- colnames(ciber_cells_collapse[2:27])

col_means_aftercollapse <- colMeans(ciber_cells_collapse[, 2:27], na.rm = TRUE)
col_means_aftercollapse = as.data.frame(col_means_aftercollapse)
col_means_aftercollapse$cell_type <- rownames(col_means_aftercollapse)

percent_detected_aftercollapse <- sapply(cell_type_collapse, function(col_name) {
  sum(ciber_cells_collapse[[col_name]] != 0, na.rm = TRUE) / length(ciber_cells_collapse[[col_name]]) * 100
})

percent_detected_aftercollapse <- data.frame(
  cell_type = cell_type_collapse,
  percent_detected = percent_detected_aftercollapse
) %>%
  left_join(col_means_aftercollapse, by = "cell_type")

percent_detected_aftercollapse$percent_detected[is.nan(percent_detected_aftercollapse$percent_detected)] <- 0

percent_detected_aftercollapse <- percent_detected_aftercollapse %>%
  arrange(percent_detected) %>%
  dplyr::rename(mean_prop=col_means_aftercollapse) %>%
  mutate(mean_percent = mean_prop * 100)

# Save Percent Detected after Collapse
#write_csv(percent_detected_aftercollapse, "/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/CellTypes_PercentDetected_AfterCollapse_N635_sPTB_CANDLEGAPPS_122325.csv")
```

Going to calculate a coefficient of variation to see which cell types relative to their percent of the composition are most variable.
```{r cell type variability}
column_sd <- apply(ciber_cells_collapse[,2:27], 2, sd)

column_mean <- apply(ciber_cells_collapse[,2:27], 2, mean)

#CV calculate
CV <- column_sd/column_mean
print(CV)

CV_df <- data.frame(CV)
```

### Remove low detection cell types
Removing cell types that are detected in less than 20% of participants.
```{r remove low detection cell types}
# We remove cell types that are detected in less than 20% of participants. 
less_than_20 = percent_detected_aftercollapse %>% 
  filter(percent_detected<20) %>% 
  pull(cell_type)

#Combine covariates and cell proportions 
data = ciber_cells_collapse %>% 
  inner_join(CANDLE_GAPPS_sPTB_FinalCovars) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-all_of(less_than_20))

#Pull just the cell types with detection greater than 20%
ciber_cells3 = ciber_cells_collapse %>% 
  dplyr::select(-all_of(less_than_20), -pathways_id) 
```

### Plot Cell Proportions
plot pre transformations and filtering
```{r plot cell propostions}
#Clean the input data and filter to only participants with full covariates (N=635)
ciber_cells_long <-ciber_cells_collapse %>% 
  pivot_longer(all_of(cell_type_collapse), names_to = "composition", 
               values_to = "value")

ciber_cells_long <- ciber_cells_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(ciber_cells_long$pathways_id %in% CANDLE_GAPPS_sPTB_FinalCovars$pathways_id)


ciber_cells_long = ciber_cells_long %>% 
  mutate(composition = ifelse(composition %in% less_than_20, paste0(composition, " (<20%)"), composition))


ciber_cells_long$composition <- gsub("_", " ", ciber_cells_long$composition) # remove underscores from cell type names

#order based on most to least proportion fetal_syncytiotrophoblast (which is most abundant cell type)
ordered_ids <- ciber_cells_long %>%
  filter(composition == "fetal syncytiotrophoblast") %>%
  arrange(desc(value)) %>%
  pull(pathways_id)

ciber_cells_long$pathways_id <- factor(ciber_cells_long$pathways_id, levels = ordered_ids)

#order based on most to least prevalent cell types
composition_order <- ciber_cells_long %>%
  group_by(composition) %>% 
  summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(mean)) %>% 
  pull(composition)

# Reorder the composition column in the entire data based on the ordering
ciber_cells_long$composition <- factor(ciber_cells_long$composition, levels = composition_order)

p_all = ggplot(ciber_cells_long, aes(x = pathways_id, y = value, fill = composition)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(x = "Participant", y = "Placental Cell Type Composition") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "H") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title = "Cell Type", ncol = 1)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) {
    index_vals <- seq(50, length(x), by = 50)  # hackey way to keep ordered factor
    labels <- rep("", length(x))  # for pathways id while adding
    labels[index_vals] <- as.character(index_vals)  # numbers to ticks
    labels})
  

p_all

```

### Save Unimputed Data
```{r save}
ciber_cells3$pathways_id <- ciber_cells_collapse$pathways_id
ciber_cells3 <- as.data.frame(ciber_cells3)
rownames(ciber_cells3) <- ciber_cells3$pathways_id
ciber_cells3 <- ciber_cells3 %>%
  dplyr::select(-pathways_id)
#save(ciber_cells3, file="/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/DeconvolutionData/Filtered_CellProportions_AfterCollapse_NoImputations_N635_sPTB_122325.RData")
```

### Run Imputation and set detection limits
```{r imputation and detection limits}
# need detection limit. says to set to 0 for variables with no LOD problems. set to min detected for those with 0s, and 0 for those with no 0s....
get_min_or_non_zero <- function(col) {
  col_min <- min(col, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (col_min == 0) {
    # Get smallest non-zero value
    non_zero_vals <- col[col != 0]
    if (length(non_zero_vals) > 0) {
      return(min(non_zero_vals, na.rm = TRUE))
    } else {
      return(0)  # In case there are no non-zero values, return 0
    }
  } else {
    return(0)  # If the min is not 0, return 0
  }
}

detection_limits <- apply(ciber_cells3, 2, get_min_or_non_zero)
view(detection_limits)
detection_limits<- unname(detection_limits)
##### check a couple to make sure it worked.
ciber_cells3 %>% filter(fetal_mesenchymal_stem_cells>0) %>% summarise(min = min(fetal_mesenchymal_stem_cells))
ciber_cells3 %>% filter( fetal_naive_cd8_t_cells>0) %>% summarise(min = min( fetal_naive_cd8_t_cells))
# fetal cytotrophoblasts has a non 0 min and was properly set to 0
ciber_cells3 %>% summarise(min = min(fetal_cytotrophoblasts))

# Run Imputation. 0s are imputed below the min detected value for each cell type.

set.seed(2025)
ciber_cells_impute = imputeBDLs(x = ciber_cells3, dl = detection_limits, maxit=50,eps=0.1,R=50,method="pls", variation=F)

#save(ciber_cells_impute, file="/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/DeconvolutionData/ciber_cells_imputationwithcollapse_N635_sPTB_122325.RData")

# Read in the imputed data (to save time by not running again- current version 11/25/25)
load("/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/DeconvolutionData/ciber_cells_imputationwithcollapse_N635_sPTB_122325.RData")
ciber_cells_impute_res = ciber_cells_impute$x

# rows do not sum to 1 as expected. acomp() on the data will transform these in a relative manner so that they sum to 100%
rowSums(ciber_cells_impute_res)

# add back pathways_id
ciber_cells_impute_res$pathways_id <- rownames(ciber_cells3)

#Save Version with pathways IDs for regressions
#save(ciber_cells_impute_res, file="/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/DeconvolutionData/ImputedCellProportions_withCollapse_CANDLEGAPPS_N635_sPTB_122325.RData")

```

### Plot Cell Proportions after Imputation

```{r plot after imputation}
# reduce our cell_types variable to only include retained cell types
cell_types <- colnames(ciber_cells_impute_res)[colnames(ciber_cells_impute_res) != "pathways_id"]

# acomp is relative composition method, now all rows should sum to 1
outcome <- compositions::acomp(ciber_cells_impute_res[,cell_types])
rowSums(outcome)

# this plots the imputed and transformed via acomp data
ciber_cells_long <- as.data.frame(outcome)
ciber_cells_long$pathways_id <-  rownames(ciber_cells3)
ciber_cells_long <- ciber_cells_long %>% 
  pivot_longer(all_of(cell_types), names_to = "composition", 
               values_to = "value")
#remove _ from cell types names
ciber_cells_long$composition <- gsub("_", " ", ciber_cells_long$composition)

#order based on most to least proportion fetal_syncytiotrophoblast
ordered_ids <- ciber_cells_long %>%
  filter(composition == "fetal syncytiotrophoblast") %>%
  arrange(desc(value)) %>%
  pull(pathways_id)

ciber_cells_long$pathways_id <- factor(ciber_cells_long$pathways_id, levels = ordered_ids)

#order based on most to least prevalent cell types
composition_order <- ciber_cells_long %>%
  group_by(composition) %>% 
  summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(mean)) %>% 
  pull(composition)

#save(composition_order, file="/Volumes/paquette_a/slapehn/CellProportions_CANDLE_GAPPS/Data/DeconvolutionData/composition_order_aftercollapse_N635_sPTB_122325.RData")

# Reorder the composition column in the entire data based on the ordering
ciber_cells_long$composition <- factor(ciber_cells_long$composition, levels = composition_order)


p_filtered = ggplot(ciber_cells_long, aes(x = pathways_id, y = value, fill = composition)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 1) +  # Ensures stacked bars with no gap
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(x = "Participant", y = "Placental Cell Type Composition") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "H") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title = "Cell Type"))+
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) {
    index_vals <- seq(50, length(x), by = 50)  # hackey way to keep ordered factor
    labels <- rep("", length(x))  # for pathways id while adding
    labels[index_vals] <- as.character(index_vals)  # numbers to ticks
    labels
  })

p_filtered

```

### Histogram of Cell Type Values
Checking that Cells types meet beta regression requirements 
```{r cell type histograms}
composition_order_underscores <- gsub(" ", "_", composition_order)
data_long2 <- data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(cell_types), names_to = "cell_type", values_to = "value")%>%
  mutate(cell_type = factor(cell_type, levels = composition_order_underscores))
ggplot(data_long2, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~cell_type, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Cell Type Values",
       x = "Value",
       y = "Count")

# double check that all cell types satisfy betaregression (0,1) distribution, no values of 1 or 0
data_long2 %>% filter(value == 1)
data_long2 %>% filter(value == 0)
data_long2 %>% filter(value > 1)
data_long2 %>% filter(value < 0)
```
